official.deadline_note: Applications must REACH the Secretary by 3.00 p.m. Monday 1 February 2027, so a posted application has to arrive, not just be sent, by that time.
official.status_note: The application form for the 2027 academic year is published and applications close on 1 February 2027; the Federation states applications for the 2026 academic year have closed and lists the five successful 2026 applicants.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Foundation publishes that it offers 'financial assistance to provide training opportunities' and that scholarships are granted 'depending on the need and cost of the course being undertaken'; it does not publish a tuition-specific coverage statement.

Recipients that are successful in any one year can apply again in any subsequent year
Open to study in New Zealand or anywhere in the South Pacific region
Financial assistance is provided to cover training opportunities for students in New Zealand and the South Pacific region

Born in the South Pacific region, which not only includes the island nations of the Pacific but also New Zealand and Australia
Students born in the South Pacific wishing to study in New Zealand or anywhere in the South Pacific are eligible
Must hold evidence of acceptance on an accredited educational or training course in the year in which they are applying (NZQA if in New Zealand)

Evidence of having been accepted onto the accredited educational or training course in the year of applying (NZQA if in New Zealand)
A full budget for the total cost of the course
The amount of financial contribution the applicant is prepared to make, and any other financial assistance available to them
A current C.V. (include a stamped addressed envelope if it must be returned)
A current character reference from a responsible citizen, dated not more than 2 years old
Applications will not be accepted without a completed official application form plus the information outlined in the Conditions for Application
Successful applicants agree to report by 31 December on the outcome of their studies for the year

Course outline with the benefits to be derived from completing the course
Evidence of acceptance onto the accredited course for the year of study (NZQA if in New Zealand)
Full budget for the total cost of the course
Statement of the applicant's own financial contribution and any other financial assistance available
Current C.V. (stamped addressed enclosure if return is required)
Character reference from a responsible citizen, not more than 2 years old

coverage: Financial assistance to provide training opportunities for students in New Zealand and the South Pacific region
Up to $1,000 a year, sized according to the need and cost of the course being undertaken

application_method: Download and read the BWM 2 Conditions of Application, which outline everything that must accompany the form
Complete the official BWM 1 application form for the 2027 academic year
Attach all papers required by the Conditions of Application
Email the signed application to exec@wi.org.nz, or post it to Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation Trust, P O Box 137, Wellington 6140, so it reaches the Secretary by 3.00 p.m. Monday 1 February 2027
official.application_route: Download the official BWM1 form and BWM2 conditions from the Federation's scholarship page, attach the full set of required papers, and email to exec@wi.org.nz or post to the Wellington address, arriving before 3.00 p.m. on 1 February 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: Birthplace-based: applicants must have been born in the South Pacific region, which the Foundation defines as the island nations of the Pacific as well as New Zealand and Australia. No citizenship or residency rule beyond birthplace is published.
official.international_eligibility: Eligible regardless of nationality, provided the applicant was born in the South Pacific region (Pacific island nations, New Zealand or Australia) and will study in New Zealand or anywhere in the South Pacific.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any accredited educational or training course (NZQA-accredited if in New Zealand); no field of study restriction is published.
official.duration: Annual award; recipients successful in any one year can apply again in any subsequent year
official.description: The Foundation was established to commemorate the life and work of the late Barbara Wood MBE, Dominion President of the NZ Federation of Country Women's Institutes 1970-1974, who died in the Mt Erebus air disaster. The Foundation offers financial assistance to provide training opportunities for students in New Zealand and the South Pacific region, with scholarships of up to $1,000 a year granted according to need and course cost at the discretion of the Trustees.
official.region: New Zealand and the South Pacific region (Oceania)
official.program_type: Charitable trust scholarship administered by the New Zealand Federation of Women's Institutes

not_confirmed: whether the award may be spent on living costs (only course need and cost are published)
verification.notes: Amount (up to $1,000 NZD a year), eligibility, 1 February 2027 3.00 p.m. deadline and the full document list were taken from the Federation's own scholarship page and its BWM2 Conditions of Application document on wi.org.nz.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a small, need-based top-up grant of up to NZD 1,000 a year, not a full scholarship, so treat it as one line in your wider funding plan. The 2027 round is open with a hard cut-off of 3.00 p.m. on 1 February 2027, and the application only counts when the signed BWM1 form plus every paper in the BWM2 conditions has reached the Secretary by email or post. Winning students can reapply in later years, so an unsuccessful or partial award this round is worth repeating next cycle.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A tertiary student born in the Pacific Islands, New Zealand or Australia, studying at any accredited institution in New Zealand or the wider South Pacific, whose course costs demonstrably exceed their own resources.
application_readiness_checklist: Download the BWM2 Conditions and the BWM1 form from the Federation's scholarship page well before February, since both documents must be completed and collated
Request a character reference early and check its date is less than 2 years old on the day you apply
Build a full annual budget of your total course cost before writing the form, since the trustees set the amount from it
Secure your acceptance letter (NZQA evidence if studying in New Zealand) so eligibility can be evidenced
Calculate the contribution you can make yourself and list every other grant or loan you hold
Send by email to exec@wi.org.nz rather than post if February approaches, so arrival before 3.00 p.m. is guaranteed
common_rejection_risks: Arriving late: the deadline is a receipt deadline (reach the Secretary by 3.00 p.m.), so a couriered or posted application that lands on 2 February fails
Missing attachments: applications without the completed official form plus every paper listed in the Conditions of Application are not accepted at all
A character reference older than 2 years, or a CV that is not current
No full course budget, or no statement of the applicant's own contribution and other assistance, leaving the trustees no basis to size the award
Applying without evidence of acceptance onto an accredited course for the year in question
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond a maximum NZD 1,000 per year: tuition fees, living costs, travel and any equipment remain the applicant's responsibility, as the award is discretionary and sized to course need and cost.
document_audit: Character reference must be dated within the last 2 years and come from a 'responsible citizen', not a family member
Include a stamped, addressed envelope with the CV only if you need documents returned
The course outline must state the benefits of completing the course, not just list papers
Evidence of acceptance must be for the year you are applying for, not a previous enrolment
alerts: Recipients must report by 31 December on the outcome of their studies for the year, so award-holders need to keep track of their results
Outcomes of the current round only arrive by 31 March 2027, after the academic year has begun, so do not rely on the grant for first-semester costs
The amount is not guaranteed: only 'up to $1,000 a year' is published and it depends on need and course cost
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email or post the signed BWM1 form with all required attachments so it reaches the Secretary by 3.00 p.m. on 1 February 2027; trustees decide in February/March and notify successful applicants by 31 March 2027.

official.deadline_note: The Trust publishes no late applications and no next opening date on its own site; the application form link was unavailable after 11.59 p.m. on Tuesday 25 August 2026.
official.status_note: The Trust's Education Awards page states 'Applications are CLOSED' and that all applications will receive a response in October 2026; the FAQ confirms the application form closed at 11.59 p.m. on Tuesday 25 August 2026 and that late applications are not accepted.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Trust describes Education Awards as 'Awards to help with study or living expenses' and publishes no tuition-specific coverage statement.
benefits: An annual programme of sponsored financial awards to help cover the costs associated with pursuing education
Awards to help with study or living expenses, for women engaged in tertiary education or trade training
Value set by NZQA level: $1000 at levels 3-4, $1500 at levels 5-6 and $3000 at level 7

Targeted Education Awards for refugee and/or migrant women, women studying STEM subjects at degree level, women studying for a trade qualification or in an apprenticeship, solo parents studying at degree level after secondary education curtailed by teen motherhood, Pasifika women studying Early Childhood or Primary Education at any level, women studying in non-traditional fields, and women who have displayed community leadership
Applicants may apply for all awards they meet the criteria for, including Personal Growth awards in addition to an Education Award
eligibility: Enrolled in an NZQA or Universities NZ approved tertiary qualification for study in 2027, with all fields of study welcome
A New Zealand citizen, or ordinarily resident in New Zealand and either having lived here on a resident-class visa for at least three years, or a refugee or protected person of New Zealand
Studying at Certificate level (NZQCF level 3-4), Diploma level (NZQCF level 5-6) or Degree level (NZQCF level 7)
Have not previously received a New Horizons for Women Trust: Hine Kahukura award at the level of study being applied for
Not enrolled in secondary school at the time of applying, unless enrolled at a secondary school as an adult student
Not for postgraduate study; the Trust directs postgraduate researchers to its separate Research Awards
Awards are only for study at NZQA approved institutions in Aotearoa New Zealand
requirements: Successful applicants must provide certified evidence of their 2027 course enrolment and ID prior to receiving the money associated with their award
Applicants must not previously have received a Trust award at the level of study being applied for
The online application must be fully submitted: a confirmation message in the web browser and a confirmation email are issued when an application is successfully submitted
documents: Certified evidence of 2027 course enrolment, required before payment
Certified identity evidence, required before payment
Online application form as specified by the Trust for the round (form link published on the Education Awards page while open)
selection_criteria: Academic potential and commitment to education: the Trust states it is not looking for perfect grades but values determination and potential to successfully complete the programme of study
Background information: reasons for returning to education and future study or employment goals
Impact of the award: how the award will contribute to the applicant's success
Applications are assessed by a minimum of three panelists; the best applications are shortlisted and then assessed by another two panelists who assign the awards
The Trust does not provide feedback on applications
coverage: Awards to help with study or living expenses
$1000 for study at NZQCF levels 3-4, $1500 at levels 5-6, $3000 at level 7
The value of awards may differ from year to year depending on the funds available
application_method: Monitor the Trust's Education Awards page for the next opening date, since the site publishes none yet
When the round opens, complete the Trust's online application form linked from the Education Awards page
Confirm submission via the browser confirmation message and the confirmation email (checking junk/spam folders)
If successful, supply certified evidence of 2027 course enrolment and ID before the award money is paid
official.application_route: Online application form published on the Trust's Education Awards page when a round is open; the 2026 round closed at 11.59 p.m. on 25 August 2026 and no reopening date is published.
official.citizenship_residency: New Zealand citizen, or ordinarily resident in New Zealand having lived here on a resident-class visa for at least three years, or a refugee or protected person of New Zealand.
official.international_eligibility: International students are not the target group: eligibility requires New Zealand citizenship, at least three years' residence on a resident-class visa, or refugee/protected-person status, and the study itself must be at an NZQA approved institution in Aotearoa New Zealand.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of study are welcome; targeted award streams exist for refugee and/or migrant women, women studying STEM at degree level, trade and apprenticeship students, solo parents at degree level, Pasifika women studying Early Childhood or Primary Education at any level, women in non-traditional fields, and women who have displayed community leadership.
official.duration: One-off award for a single qualification; a previous recipient cannot apply again at the same level of study
official.description: New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura offers an annual programme of sponsored financial awards to help cover the costs associated with pursuing education. The awards support women who are returning to education or continuing their educational journey, especially those whose path to learning has not been straightforward, and who have faced and overcome challenges and shown commitment to education, training or personal development.
official.program_type: Annual programme of sponsored education grants from a New Zealand charitable trust, with targeted streams

verification.notes: Values ($1000/$1500/$3000 by NZQCF level), closed status, 25 August 2026 11.59 p.m. deadline, certified-evidence pre-payment condition, selection criteria and panel process were all taken from the Trust's own Education Awards, FAQs and Awards pages.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-off grant of NZD 1,000 to NZD 3,000 sized by your NZQCF level, not a full scholarship, so budget for the rest of your fees and living costs yourself. The current round closed at 11.59 p.m. on 25 August 2026 with all applicants to receive an email decision in October 2026, so the practical move now is to prepare a certified enrolment and ID pack for the next round. Note the one-award-per-level rule: if you already held a Trust award at certificate, diploma or degree level, you cannot apply again at that same level.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A New Zealand citizen or long-term resident woman re-entering certificate, diploma or degree study at an NZQA-approved New Zealand institution, especially a returning student, refugee or migrant woman, or a Pasifika woman entering Early Childhood or Primary Education.
application_readiness_checklist: Watch the Education Awards page for the next opening date, as the Trust publishes no schedule in advance
Get certified copies of your 2027 course enrolment and photo ID ready now, since payment only follows certified evidence
Map your qualification to its NZQCF level (3-4, 5-6 or 7) to know whether you are applying for $1,000, $1,500 or $3,000

Identify which targeted stream fits you (refugee/migrant, STEM degree, trade or apprenticeship, solo parent, Pasifika Early Childhood or Primary Education, non-traditional field, community leadership) and reflect it in your answers
Check you have never held a Trust award at the same level of study before investing time in the form
Draft your story around your return to education and future study or employment goals, which the panel explicitly scores
common_rejection_risks: Applying at postgraduate level or for study at an institution outside New Zealand, both of which the Trust excludes outright
Having previously received a Trust award at the same level of study being applied for
Being enrolled in secondary school at the time of applying, unless enrolled as an adult student
Submitting late: the form link switches off at 11.59 p.m. on the closing date and no late applications are accepted
Failing to supply certified enrolment and ID evidence after selection, which blocks payment of the award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The grant is a one-off payment, so all tuition, living, travel and study costs beyond NZD 1,000-$3,000, plus the cost of certifying enrolment and identity documents, remain the applicant's own.
document_audit: Certification means copies certified by a JP, solicitor or similar, not plain photocopies or phone photos
Enrolment evidence must be for 2027 study, so time your application and evidence around your confirmed 2027 enrolment
Identity evidence must also be certified and supplied before the money is released, not after
alerts: The round is currently closed and the Trust publishes no reopening date, so plan other funding for 2027 in parallel
Outcome emails can land in junk or spam folders; the Trust confirms notification by email by the end of October 2026
No application feedback is provided, so you cannot request panel comments to improve a future application
Award values may change year to year depending on funds available, so the $1,000/$1,500/$3,000 tiers are not guaranteed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the Trust's online form when a round opens, watch for the browser confirmation and confirmation email, then supply certified 2027 enrolment and ID evidence before payment if selected.
